content.text: The document expressly negates minimum commitments; no take-or-pay exposure exists.

input.quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
input.rationale: The agreement meets the preferred position: § 2.1 (p0012) expressly disclaims any minimum quantity or purchase commitment, limits our payment obligation to Services actually ordered under an executed Order Form, and confirms that declining to place further orders is neither a breach nor a shortfall. § 7.1 (p0026) reinforces this by barring Vendor from imposing minimum-use or similar charges not identified in the Order Form, and § 12.3 (p0050) records that we have given no minimum-volume, exclusivity, or MFC commitment. No take-or-pay, shortfall penalty, forecast obligation, or volume cap on our usage appears anywhere. The only "shortfall" references (§§ 22.2–22.3) are usage-audit true-ups for under-reported consumption, which is the true-up mechanic the playbook prefers, not a penalty. The § 7.6 liquidated damages for dependency delay is a separate commercial term addressed under the LD rule and is not a purchase commitment. No redline needed.
